title: Who is left with more marbles, Jia or Ruhee?
description: Two differences are compared without working out either one, by imagining two children who each lose some marbles. Keeko doubts the answer and thinks the child who starts with more must end with more.
teaching_notes: One idea: when both numbers of a difference move together, the difference can stay the same. Watch for children who think the bigger starting number always leaves more.

video_script.why: The child sees that two differences can match when both numbers shift by the same amount.
video_script.substitution: Imagine two children who each lose some marbles, and compare the start and the loss.
video_script.anchor: Jia and Ruhee with their marbles, before and after losing some
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the child who starts with more marbles must end with more, and forgets that the same child also loses one more.
video_script.payoff_line: Jia and Ruhee are left with the same number of marbles

final_answer.spoken: one hundred thirteen minus twenty five is the same as one hundred twelve minus twenty four

names.Jia: the child who had 113 marbles and lost 25
names.Ruhee: the child who had 112 marbles and lost 24

maths_rules: 1 − 1 = 0, so they are left with the same number
video_script.design: One idea: both numbers move by the same amount, so the difference stays. Assumes taking away. Wrong idea: starting with more means ending with more. The two children and their marbles stay all video.
